newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude prices dip in Asia, Minas seen firming a bit.
newsitem.headline: Crude prices dip in Asia, Minas seen firming a bit.

text.p: Crude oil prices fell in Asia on Tuesday, while in the wet market January Minas was seen firming and some February light Gulf grades were attracting strong premiums, traders said.
January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.45/22.55, in line with the SIMEX futures market.

In the wet market, trade in light Gulf crudes for February lifting has started with the crude fetching strong premiums comparable to, or even higher than January cargoes, traders said. A February Qatar Land was rumoured to have been sold to a South Korean refinery at QGPC plus 52 or 53 cents.

A second February Qatar Land cargo was rumoured to have been sold by a Japanese trader to a Japanese refiner at QGPC plus 55 cents. Two other Qatari crudes were also believed to have been sold recently. These included a January Al Rayyan, which was believed to have been sold to a South Korean refinery at Arab Heavy minus 60-80 cents and a cargo of January Al Shaheen was believed to have been sold to a U.S. major at Dubai-linked quotes plus 80 cents.
A February Murban was rumoured to have traded hands at ADNOC plus 71 cents. Oman cut the price of its crude lifted in November by 70 cents a barrel to $21.80.
